column1: # Device metrics no LOINC code fits, grouped by the reason, because the reason decides what to do.
#   ALGO_MISMATCH      LOINC has the concept but codes another algorithm (HRV: SDNN only, five vendors publish RMSSD)
#   VENDOR_SCORE       a proprietary score; LOINC does not code these and never will
#   NO_CONCEPT         the concept is absent from the axis table
#   UNIT_INCOMPARABLE  a near code exists but the vendor's unit or weighting makes the number incomparable
#   RELATIVE           a deviation from a baseline, not an absolute quantity
#   NOT_MEASUREMENT    a goal, a recommendation or a plan
#   QUALITY_META       a data-quality or device-state signal; worth keeping beside the reading, not as one
#   OUT_OF_SCOPE       raw waveforms, location, nutrition: outside this catalogue
# Columns: reason, metric (the quantity as vendors name it), vendors (who publishes it, with
# their field names), detail (the evidence), disposition (what the catalogue does).
# Read 2026-09-09 against LOINC 2.83; the notes were translated from Chinese in 1.5.1.

column4: Every HRV code in LOINC 2.83 is of SDNN descent (112429-6 SDNN, 76643-6 and 80404-7 R-R interval.standard deviation). The axis table has 0 hits for `RMSSD`. SDNN is the standard deviation of all NN intervals, RMSSD the root mean square of successive differences: different definitions, not interchangeable. Six vendors publish RMSSD, only Apple publishes SDNN
column5: Keep in the `hrvRMSSD` device namespace, no code. This is the one entry worth filing a new-code request with Regenstrief. Garmin's beat-to-beat RR series allows computing SDNN, which may carry 112429-6 as long as the method records that it was computed here
